changes: - Universal deformable vehicle mesh replaces the legacy-loft `CarShapeParams` presets in the hint path: one fixed-topology, left/right-symmetric body (18 stations x 20-vertex rings, planar bevelled end caps, an open bed cavity) whose side silhouette is piecewise linear between semantic landmarks (tail, rear-window base, roof rear, roof front, windshield base, nose). Shape hints are 30 floats: schema 2.0, type index, 28 profile values.

- Seven body types (sedan, hatchback, crossover, full_suv, minivan, van, pickup) with metric archetype priors normalized per box. Detector boxes are modeled as vehicle + (0.30, 0.36, 0.32) m, so roofs and sides are no longer pinned to the inflated box.

- `VehicleShapeFitter`: ring-plane residual with planar caps and a slope correction (held-out scoring here uses true point-to-triangle distance); Huber 8 cm clamped at 25 cm inside / 30 cm outside (through-glass interior returns, motion smear); each type fit within 2 sigma of its prior; data strength saturates at 300 voxels; unconstrained parameters frozen. Sweeps screen every type with a 2-iteration fit, refine the best 3 plus the incumbent, and compare 0.25 x data + parameter prior + box-dimension NLL with a 15% switch margin; other refits only refit the incumbent (as live).
- Underside rises 0.2 m over each overhang (bumpers above rockers), so wheels show from behind and ahead.
- Before the first accepted fit the dimension-prior type mean is published ("prior only"), so sparse far vehicles get a type-appropriate proxy instead of the legacy primitive.
- Renders: legacy primitive, type mean and fitted shape all carry the same published tint.

- Known data issue: moving cars' accumulated returns are smeared ~0.5 m along x, and in agent-2 frames the frame-t LiDAR belt samples project ahead of the car in the image (camera/LiDAR sync in the dataset, not the harness).

callouts.note: red Tesla sedan: must not regress
